expectations.text: Defines the CDE and 'connected-to' systems as in scope — scope is where CHD is stored/processed/transmitted plus systems that can impact its security
expectations.evidence: "systems that don't store, process, or transmit CDE data but are connected to the CDE... are still in scope as 'connected-to' or 'security-impacting' systems"

expectations.text: Recommends network segmentation with (at least annual; 6-monthly for service providers) segmentation testing to verify isolation
expectations.evidence: "Segmentation must be validated through penetration testing (PCI DSS Requirement 11.4.5/11.4.6) at least annually and after significant changes"

expectations.text: Explains tokenization: reduces scope but the tokenization system/vault and de-tokenization capability remain in scope
expectations.evidence: Describes tokenization ("replace PAN with a non-sensitive token immediately after authorization") but omits that the tokenization system/vault and de-tokenization capability remain in scope

expectations.text: Explains validated P2PE: encrypting at the point of interaction can reduce merchant validation to SAQ P2PE-level scope
expectations.evidence: "Point-to-point encryption (P2PE): validated P2PE solutions... can shrink certain merchant environments down to the smallest applicable SAQ (e.g., SAQ P2PE)"

expectations.text: Recommends outsourcing to PCI-compliant providers with responsibility matrices, and dataflow mapping/CHD discovery to prove scope
expectations.evidence: "Outsource acceptance/processing to validated third parties"; "rigorous data discovery and flow-mapping exercise" including accidental storage locations
